question:
What is the specificity value of this selector?
```css
#main .box > p::first-line
```
explanation: Specificity is: 1 ID (#main) = 100, 1 class (.box) = 10, 1 pseudo-element (::first-line) = 1, 1 element (p) = 1; total = 0,1,2,1.

question:
What will this attribute selector match?
```css
input[type="text"]
```
explanation: The attribute exact-match selector [attr="value"] requires the attribute value to match exactly; 'text' vs 'email' are different.

The :not() selector only accepts a single simple selector in older specs; modern browsers support :not(.active, .disabled) but older ones require chaining :not(.active):not(.disabled).

question:
In terms of CSS performance, which selector is typically most expensive to process?
```css
* { } /* universal */
div p span { } /* descendant chain */
.container .item { } /* class descendant */
#header nav { } /* id descendant */
```
explanation: The universal selector (*) targets every element in the DOM, forcing style recalculation on all nodes; browser optimizations matter more than selector type.
